text.author: Rajiva Wijesinha
text.title: Letter from SCOPP Secretary General Rajiva Wijesinha to the International Herald Tribune 20 - 08 - 2007
text.summary1: (human1) Rajiva Wijesinja, the Secretary General of Sri Lanka, writes to the editor of the International Herald Tribune regarding an article by Charu Hogg on the human rights situation in Sri Lanka indiscriminate attacks by the government which led to the displacement and forced return of people, stating that her claims were exaggerated and being used to promote the opposition.
text.summary2: (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) In a letter to the International Herald Tribune, Sri Lankan Secretary General Rajiva Wijesinha challenges Charu Hogg's Human Rights Watch article on Sri Lanka, arguing her claims exaggerate civilian casualties, ignore evidence of voluntary refugee returns, and align with opposition and LTTE efforts to destabilize the democratically-elected government.
text.summary3: (gpt4o; postedited) In a letter to the International Herald Tribune, Rajiva Wijesinha criticizes Charu Hogg's article on Sri Lanka’s human rights situation, arguing it unfairly aligns with LTTE and opposition agendas, overlooks government efforts, and employs exaggerations, while also cautioning against destabilizing the democratically elected government.
text.summary4: (Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct) A letter to the Editor of the International Herald Tribune critiques an article by Charu Hogg on Sri Lanka's human rights situation, arguing that her claims are exaggerated and aligned with the interests of the LTTE and opposition party.
text.summary5: (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) Rajiva Wijesinha disputes Charu Hogg's IHT article on Sri Lanka's human rights situation, arguing it contains exaggerations and conflates with terrorist and opposition agendas, while emphasizing the voluntary nature of returns and the government's handling of the conflict.
